chunks: And by this chain, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you stand from the Rak'ah, rely upon your palms and say, "By the Might of Allah and His Strength, I stand and sit," for Ali (peace be upon him) used to do that.'
ai.seo_question: What should one say and do when standing up from the first Rak'ah in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the prophetic tradition of attributing physical capability in prayer to divine sustenance, specifically linking the practice to Imam Ali (AS) as a model of piety. It underscores the Shia emphasis on imitating the Ahl al-Bayt in ritual details, transforming a physical movement into an act of conscious gratitude and reliance on Allah's power (quwwah) and provision (quwwah).
